# Copilot instructions

Guidance for AI agents working in this repository.

## Language

- **Use English only** in code, comments, docstrings, documentation, commit messages and
  chat answers. Do not introduce other languages.

## What this repository is

A sandbox for driving **Rigby2D** (2D skeletal animation) over the **Model Context Protocol**:
a sample character project, an unpacked copy of the Rigby2D MCP server, and a Python demo client.

```
add_arms_up.py              demo script: adds the "arms up" animation, input/ -> output/
rigby2d_mcp_utils.py           reusable MCP client: transport, RunLog, discovery, paths
input/test.rigby               sample project ("NILA"); read-only source
output/test.rigby              generated by the script; never edit by hand
logs/                          generated: one run-<timestamp>.log per run
_tools/mcp-server/             Rigby2D MCP server 0.5.0 (Node.js, self-contained)
_tools/start_mcpServer.bat     Windows launcher
run_add_animation.bat          convenience wrapper around the demo script
_INFO/                         reference only: upstream sources/docs, .mcpb, original project
```

## Hard rules

1. **Never edit `.rigby` files by hand.** They are multi-megabyte JSON with embedded images,
   rewritten atomically by the editor and the MCP tools. All changes go through MCP tools.
2. **`input/` is the source, `output/` and `logs/` are generated.** The script must read only
   from `input/` and write only to `output/` (MCP `output:` + `overwrite: true`), so the source
   project stays byte-identical. Never write generated files to the repository root.
3. **Never move files across `_tools/`, `_INFO/`, `input/` and the repository root** unless the
   task says so. The root holds the runnable script and the project folders.
4. **Never add runtime dependencies to the Python scripts** — standard library only.
   The Node server's dependencies live in `_tools/mcp-server/node_modules` (git-ignored).
5. **Do not commit** `input/`, `output/`, `logs/`, `_INFO/`, `node_modules/`, `.venv/`,
   `_preview/`, `*.mcpb` or `*.backup.rigby`. `.gitignore` covers them: the repository tracks
   the code and the server, the project data and the upstream reference stay local.
6. **Back up before a destructive batch.** The MCP tools keep no history and save in place;
   `output/` is the scratch copy. Edits to `input/` need a copy in `_INFO/backups/` first.

## Running things

The MCP server is not on PATH and `node` may not be on PATH either; the demo script locates
both itself (path overrides: `NODE_EXE`, `RIGBY_MCP_SERVER`, `RIGBY_WORKSPACE`).

```powershell
# smoke test: adds "arms_up" to input/test.rigby and verifies output/test.rigby
python add_arms_up.py
python add_arms_up.py input/test.rigby build/other.rigby   # explicit paths

# server CLI (stdio transport)
node _tools\mcp-server\src\mcp\server.js --help
node _tools\mcp-server\src\mcp\server.js --root .
```

A correct run prints hand positions that rise at `t=0.8` and return at `t=1.6`, ends with
`validate_project: OK`, exits with code `0` and leaves `input/test.rigby` unchanged.

## MCP facts worth remembering

- Transport: **stdio, JSON-RPC 2.0, one message per line**. Logs go to stderr. Never start
  the server through `npm run`, because npm writes to stdout.
- Methods: `initialize`, `notifications/initialized`, `ping`, `tools/list`, `tools/call`.
  Protocol revisions: `2025-06-18`, `2025-03-26`, `2024-11-05`.
- Results carry both `structuredContent` (preferred) and JSON text content.
  Tool failures return `isError: true` with an actionable message — read that text.
- Server layout: `src/mcp/protocol.js` (transport), `tools.js` (read/validate/convert),
  `edits.js` (editing), `film.js` (film/poses/audio), `rigging.js` (AutoRig/retarget),
  `scene.js`, `scripting.js` (Pyodide), on top of the runtime in `src/core`.

## Editing model

- Key values are **relative to the setup pose**: `rotate` is added in degrees, `translate`
  and `shear` add x/y, `scale` multiplies x/y. Angles are degrees, time is seconds, **Y is up**.
- `set_bone_key` takes `value` for `rotate` and `x`/`y` for the other channels.
- Curves shape the segment to the next key: `linear`, `stepped`, `easeIn`, `easeOut`,
  `easeInOut`, or a bezier `[cx1, cy1, cx2, cy2]` (CSS `cubic-bezier`).
- Animation duration grows to include new keys; there is no explicit "set duration" step.
- **Use `batch_edit`** for more than a couple of keys: one load and one atomic save.
  Operations are `{ "op": "<tool name without path/output/overwrite>", ... }` and run in order.
- Every editing tool accepts `output` (+ `overwrite`) to save a copy instead of changing the
  input. That is how the pipeline keeps `input/` intact and fills `output/`.
- **The `output` folder must already exist**: the server refuses a missing folder. The script
  creates `output/` and `logs/` before the first call.
- Verification tools: `describe_animation` (key times), `sample_pose` (world transforms at a
  time), `validate_project` (structure, images, round-trip), `export_sprite_sheet`
  (visual preview; the output folder must exist, and `overwrite: true` to replace files).

## This rig (`input/test.rigby`)

39 bones, 42 slots, 1 skin, 10 constraints, project name `NILA`.

- Hierarchy: `root > hip > chest > neck > head > (eyes, brows, nose, mouth, hair, ears, braids,
  earrings, jasmine)`, arms `chest > upperarm_(l|r) > forearm_(l|r) > hand_(l|r)`,
  legs `hip > thigh_(l|r) > shin_(l|r) > foot_(l|r)`, plus `camera`.
- IK constraints exist for both hands and feet, but **hand IK `mix` is 0** — the arms are free,
  so animate `upperarm_*` / `forearm_*` / `hand_*` directly. Foot IK `mix` is 1, so move
  `ik_foot_l` / `ik_foot_r` to pose the legs.
- Physics constraints drive `braid1..3`, `earring_l/r` and `jasmine`, so those follow the head.
- The character faces the viewer: its left (`_l` bones) appears on the image's right. Bone
  `hand_l` sits at +X (~541), `hand_r` at −X (~−541).
- Existing animations: `idle` (3 s, neck/hip/head plus an eye blink at ~1.9–2.0 s) and
  `arms_up` (1.6 s, created by the demo script).
- Film data is present even though the workspace is `game`: output 60 fps, 1920×1080,
  transparent, `camera` framing (center 0, 1560; scale 3.05); poses `Happy`, `Surprised`,
  `Thinking`; face control `Mood`; audio track `Nila_voiceover.mp3`.

## Code style for the Python tools

- Python 3.8+ syntax, standard library only, `from __future__ import annotations`.
- Type hints on functions, short docstrings, `# ---` section banners.
- **`rigby2d_mcp_utils.py` holds all MCP plumbing** (`RunLog`, `find_node`, `find_server`,
  `RigbyMcpClient`, `connect()`, path helpers, result helpers). Feature scripts import it as
  `import rigby2d_mcp_utils as mcp` and keep only their own edit logic; do not duplicate the
  transport in a new script.
- Every script takes `input` and `output` project paths through
  `mcp.add_project_arguments(parser)` + `mcp.project_paths(...)`, so paths are validated to
  stay inside the workspace, the output folder is created, and input == output is refused.
- Prefer explicit constants at the top of the file over magic numbers inside functions.
- **Always log through `RunLog`**, never with bare `print` for process output: the log file is
  the record of a run. Errors go through `log.error` and end in a non-zero exit code; the
  traceback belongs in the log, not in the user's face.
- One log file per run in `logs/`, named `run-YYYYmmdd-HHMMSS.log`, created by `RunLog`.
  Verbose tool traffic (`tools/call` arguments and results) is log-only via `log.detail`.
